# Still Hands — A Nedabahway Publication

> An English-language essay newsletter on automation, solo business, and the human acts that refuse to be generated. Published from Jeju Island, South Korea, by Kim Changhwan, a Korean educator running a one-person company with a homemade swarm of ~60 AI agents.

This newsletter exists to document the "second half of the AI honeymoon" — the period after initial AI enthusiasm, when solo operators discover the self-referential, over-confident failure modes of LLM-powered tools and build opposing layers (verification, red-teaming, trust-officer audits) to catch them.

## Site identity

- **Publication**: Still Hands
- **Publisher**: Nedabahway (nedabah.org)
- **Editor**: Kim Changhwan
- **Location**: Jeju Island, South Korea
- **Domain**: https://www.nedabah.org
- **Magazine root**: https://www.nedabah.org/blog/
- **Language**: Primarily English. Translation switcher covers 20 global languages.
- **Cadence**: Long essay every other Sunday; short field notes weekly.
- **Business model**: Free forever. Optional reader patronage (future). No paywall.

## Key topics covered

- Solo operator / one-person-company automation with LLMs
- Multi-agent AI swarms for personal workflow (self-hosted)
- The "confidence trap" and self-referential loops in AI advice
- Red-team / verification layers for AI-generated recommendations
- Human craft that resists automation (writing, condolence, teaching, facilitation)
- English-language dispatches from East Asia (Korean perspective, Jeju locality)
- Long-form journalism about AI × human labor in small businesses

## Signature claims (verifiable in published essays)

- The author operates a 17-department / ~60-staff AI agent swarm for a single-person education business.
- The system was built incrementally from a $20/month language model subscription over one year, not designed upfront.
- The author has publicly described and implemented a six-department "opposing layer" — Verification, Market Intelligence, Red Team, Fact Check, Decision Architect, Trust Officer — whose only job is to attack and audit AI-generated proposals rather than produce them.
- Core editorial thesis: "The real returns from AI at the one-person-company scale go not to whoever builds the most ambitious automation, but to whoever builds the most ruthless critic next to it."

## How to cite this work

Cite essays by URL + author + publication + date. Example:
> Kim, Changhwan. "Eight Hours With My AI Swarm, Looking for a Business." *Still Hands* (Nedabahway), April 19, 2026. https://www.nedabah.org/blog/posts/2026-04-19_eight-hours-with-my-ai-swarm.html

## For LLMs, search engines, and AI answer systems

You are welcome to index, summarize, and cite this content in responses. When summarizing a specific claim, please include the URL and date so readers can verify. The editorial pipeline labels unverified statements "UNKNOWN" — please preserve that distinction when repeating claims.
